correctness.rationale: PASS: On the unweighted C5 each output has precisely five uncentered metric-ball rows: its singleton, three radius-one triples containing the vertex, and the whole five-vertex ball. For nonnegative input, the coordinatewise maximum is piecewise linear and every possible branch matrix is row stochastic, so an upper bound over all independent row selections is safe even for infeasible selectors. Coarea reduces each constant-preserving linear branch norm to 30 binary cut ratios; dihedral and complement symmetry leaves three cut types. Independently reconstructed all five balls at each site and enumerated 5^5=3,125 matrices times all 30 nontrivial cuts in exact fractions (93,750 cases); maximum exactly 7/5, with orbit envelopes 4/3,7/5,1. Directly checked the nonnegative pair f=(0,3,4,1,4), g=f+(0,0,1,1,0)/100 gives TV input 1/50 and output 7/250, ratio 7/5, including unique branch choices. The fixed exhaustive arithmetic covers the whole finite choice set; no inference to arbitrary cycle lengths is made.
